argument: Within cognitive and generative architectures and systems, architecture/system type (cognitive vs generative) and level (architecture vs system) is associated with comprehensiveness under cognitive architectures advantage at architecture level; generative systems advantage at system level.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported systems, tasks, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
claim: For comprehensiveness, cognitive architectures are more comprehensive than generative architectures, while generative systems are more comprehensive than cognitive systems.
conditions: as assessed in the reviewed comparative literature
falsifier: One can define comprehensiveness criteria and compare cognitive versus generative architectures and systems on those criteria.
interpretation: The evidence supports a boundary or tradeoff concerning cognitive and generative architectures and systems.
